references_named: Four Seasons / Seagram Building commission, withdrawn by the artist 1959
Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
rationale: The iframe-detection (window.self !== window.top with cross-origin try/catch) is the literal enactment of Rothko's Seagram withdrawal: the mechanism refuses to be décor because it is being used as décor. The self-referential srcdoc demo — a perfect copy of the page embedded inline captioned as The Four Seasons, which then withdraws — is an elegant staging that also carries the Benjamin aura joke (mechanical reproduction identical to original, yet worthless as decoration). Concept and execution are one object. Reads cleanly at two depths. Web-only mechanism; fresh source within the catalogue.
reservations: The P5/chance claim is thin — the per-visit oxblood mix and inner-form jitter are minimal, and the dominant gesture is order (deterministic withdrawal). The Rothko CSS approximation is functional rather than evocative. The work doesn't explicitly name a prior work in the y-a-v-a catalogue it answers, only art-historical and web-historical precedents.
revision_suggestion: Strengthen the chance/order axis by making the withdrawal itself vary per visit — e.g., sometimes the painting persists a few seconds before going dark, sometimes the refusal message changes tone — so chance has real stake in the gesture, not just in the color palette. Optionally tighten the lineage to an explicit prior work (e.g., position this as a web-native answer to Tragedian's vanishing fruit or to the withdrawal gestures in Hammer Price / Inside the White Cube).
